programme: HIF1A and STAT3 act as the transcriptional core of a chronic hypoxia/oxidative-stress response that drives SNAI1-dependent epithelial-to-mesenchymal (COPD) or endothelial-to-mesenchymal (MS) transition, with JUND supplying the AP-1 stress-response arm; EGR2 separately sets the inflammatory identity of the resident myeloid population (alveolar macrophage in lung, microglia in CNS) operating in the same stressed tissue.
role_in_a: In COPD, chronic hypoxia and cigarette-smoke oxidative stress activate HIF1A and STAT3 in airway epithelium and macrophages, driving SNAI1-dependent epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition that contributes to airway wall remodeling and fibrosis, with JUND/AP-1 sustaining the oxidative-stress transcriptional programme; EGR2 independently imprints the alveolar-macrophage identity that perpetuates chronic lung inflammation.
role_in_b: In MS, a HIF1A risk variant tracks with disability and smoldering inflammation, STAT3 signaling is activated in lesion-associated glia and lymphocytes, and inflammation-induced SNAI1-dependent endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition of brain endothelial cells contributes to blood-brain-barrier breakdown; EGR2 governs the inflammatory microglial state within demyelinating lesions.
shared_axis: Both are chronic barrier-organ diseases in which sustained hypoxic/inflammatory stress locks the local barrier cell (airway epithelium vs. brain endothelium) into a HIF1A/STAT3/SNAI1 mesenchymal-transition state that degrades barrier integrity, while the tissue-resident myeloid cell (alveolar macrophage vs. microglia) adopts an EGR2-dependent inflammatory identity in the same microenvironment — a convergent barrier-injury response rather than a shared root cause.
reasoning: HIF1A, STAT3 and SNAI1 are each independently placed in COPD and in MS by multiple disease-specific papers, and two retrieved papers (35972942, 40594490) explicitly discuss HIF1A and STAT3 respectively across both diseases at once, so the connection is not purely inferred. Support is downgraded from 'established' because those joint papers are multi-disease association/signature studies rather than a dedicated COPD-MS mechanism, and JUND/EGR2 contribute tissue-specific but not directly cross-referenced evidence.
support: 37275442 (SNAI1 drives EMT in COPD airway epithelium via METTL3/m6A-SOCS3/STAT axis); 30718504 (inflammation-induced, SNAI1-associated endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition causes brain endothelial dysfunction in neuroinflammation); 42328420, 40865348, 42641443 (HIF1A implicated in COPD via Mendelian randomization, anti-inflammatory mechanism, and heavy-metal exposure studies); 41639279 (HIF1A variant affects long-term disability and smoldering inflammation in MS); 35972942 (HIF1A polymorphisms associate with risk across multiple diseases including COPD and MS); 31578304 (JUND/AP-1 oxidative-stress model of lung emphysema in COPD); 42032712, 42334931, 42634575 (STAT3 drives EMT/macrophage reprogramming/signaling in COPD lung pathology); 42002896, 42577052, 42177676 (STAT3 implicated in MS via Mendelian randomization drug-target analysis, an immunosuppressive cytokine pathway, and a STAT3-inhibitor efficacy study); 40594490 (STAT3 signaling identified as a shared pathogenic signature across multiple diseases including both); 34797692 (EGR2 required for alveolar macrophage tissue-specific imprinting in lung); 42319825 (EGR2 implicated in microglia inflammatory states during demyelination).
how_to_falsify: In parallel, expose human bronchial epithelial cells (hypoxia/cigarette-smoke extract) and human brain microvascular endothelial cells (TNF/IFN-gamma) to STAT3 inhibition (e.g. S3I-201, already validated in the MS literature here); if SNAI1 induction and mesenchymal markers (E-cadherin loss, vimentin gain) are not suppressed in both systems, the shared HIF1A/STAT3/SNAI1 axis does not hold. Separately, delete/inhibit EGR2 in alveolar macrophages and in microglia under matched inflammatory stimulation — if the myeloid inflammatory signature collapses in only one tissue, the EGR2 arm is tissue-specific rather than shared.
caveats: Tissue pairing is brain vs. lung, so any shared mechanism is inferred convergence in barrier cell types, not shared anatomy. The 338 patient-group comparisons come from only 6 independent cohort pairs, so the true replication depth is much smaller than the comparison count suggests. RUNX2 has the highest recurrence (237/338) but no MS association at all and was deliberately excluded from the carrying story — a reminder that recurrence rank does not equal disease relevance. Tissue-generic exclusions (FOXP3, STAT4, MEF2C, NRG1, ZEB1, etc.) removed the more obvious immune/neural master regulators, so the account should not be read as reaching for those; their absence is by design, not a gap. Single-view factors (BCL11A, RORB, FOXI1, etc.) were correctly left out and do not belong in this story.
